title: More Than 500 People Commemorate the Centenary of Fidel Castro’s Birth at the Cuban Embassy in Mexico
author: José Shaddai Olvera Torres
content:
_This article by José Shaddai Olvera Torres originally appeared in the[August
15, 2026 edition of El Chamuco y los Hijos del
Averno](https://elchamuco.com.mx/2026/08/15/mas-de-500-personas-conmemoran-el-
centenario-del-natalicio-de-fidel-castro-en-la-embajada-de-cuba-en-mexico),
Mexico's iconic political satire magazine._

The Cuban Embassy in Mexico commemorated this Thursday the centenary of the
birth of Commander in Chief Fidel Castro Ruz with an event that brought
together more than 500 people and that reaffirmed the historic ties of
friendship and solidarity between Cuba and Mexico.

The diplomatic mission welcomed federal deputies, representatives of the
Secretariat of Foreign Relations (SRE), members of the diplomatic corps
accredited in Mexico, the general secretary of Morena, members of the Vanegas
family, organizations and movements in solidarity with Cuba, members of the
Association of Cubans Residing in Mexico, representatives of political
parties, graduates from Cuba, business owners, journalists, academics,
intellectuals, artists, Cuban medical collaborators serving in Mexico, and
numerous friends of the island.

Representing the Mexican Foreign Secretariat, Carlos Imanol Belausteguigoitia
Reyes, director general for Central America and the Caribbean at the SRE,
emphasized that Mexico and Cuba share 124 years of relations marked by
friendship and solidarity.

The official recalled that Mexico has provided aid to Cuba and has served as a
bridge to channel humanitarian assistance from third countries. He also
recognized the capacity for struggle, solidarity, ingenuity, and resilience
demonstrated by the Cuban people throughout their history.

During the event, federal deputy Dolores Padierna, deputy coordinator of
Morena's parliamentary group in the Chamber of Deputies, highlighted the
influence of the Cuban Revolution and of Fidel Castro in Latin America, as
well as the relevance of his thought in the face of current challenges.

**" To speak of Fidel is to speak of Cuba,"** the legislator said, affirming
that the revolutionary leader's legacy remains relevant because many of the
problems he identified are still present and because the current times demand
new forms of resistance.

Padierna added that, on the hundredth anniversary of his birth, the figure of
Fidel Castro "grows larger" and continues to inspire solidarity with the Cuban
people.

For his part, the ambassador of Cuba in Mexico, Eugenio Martínez Enríquez,
took up words from the Cuban president, Miguel Díaz-Canel Bermúdez, who has
said that remembering the Commander in Chief "is not to manage nostalgia," but
because his thought remains a guide for confronting Cuba's current challenges.

The diplomat highlighted Fidel Castro's ability to anticipate historic events
and asserted that his main legacy is a people who are "dignified, noble,
brave, and in solidarity," as well as a sovereign, secure nation determined to
defend its rights.

> The sin of being free and sovereign is a hard-won right that we Cubans will
> never renounce.
>
> Eugenio Martínez Enríquez, Ambassador of Cuba in Mexico

He also thanked the president of Mexico, Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, for the
moral and material support given to Cuba, and maintained that the future of
the island will continue to be marked by resistance, struggle, and
international solidarity.

**" The flag of the lone star, high and worthy of the Cubans, cannot fall and
will not fall," the ambassador said.**

As part of the commemoration, the Cuban duo Buena Fe offered a musical
performance before those in attendance.

The ceremony concluded with a symbolic moment in which those present sang Las
Mañanitas and shared the cakes prepared to celebrate the hundred years of
Fidel Castro's birth, in a day that reaffirmed the relevance of his memory and
the attendees' commitment to solidarity between Mexico and Cuba.
